subject: EU announces plan to ban social media for under 13s | CNN
posts:
Can a government ban protect kids from the digital wild west, or does it just build a fence around everyone else? The EU's proposed under-13 social media ban raises the stakes.
Evidence: Child Safety, Mass Surveillance, Digital ID Pretext
#Aletheia #TechPolicy

The European Union claims its proposed 'EU Kids Act' will protect vulnerable children from addictive algorithms, harmful content, and predatory AI companions by banning social media for under-13s.
Stated Judgement: (+0.85, +0.80) — Greater Good

In reality, enforcing these age limits requires invasive, universal age-verification systems. This effectively mandates a digital ID for all citizens, trading privacy for paternalistic state control.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.61, +0.45) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Deception. The policy uses the genuine crisis of youth mental health as a Trojan horse to normalize mass digital surveillance and age-gating infrastructure.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 2)

- EU Kids Act: COND (-0.45, 0.35) — High surveillance risk.
- Platform Safety: FAIL (-0.75, 0.55) — Shifts burden to users.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a plan to ban social media for children under 13, introducing 'mini accounts' for 13-14 year olds and requiring platforms to prove their safety.

The Poison:
While keeping toddlers off addictive feeds is a noble goal, the infrastructure required to police this ban strips away online anonymity for adults and centralizes control over digital speech.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The Plane Error occurs between the Logical (HOW) and Physical (WHERE) planes. The EU logically argues for child safety, but physically implements a mass-surveillance regime that fails to address the root causes of tech addiction.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic Smart Selfish Maneuver. The state uses a manufactured crisis—the inability of parents to police tech—as a pretext to hoard power via digital IDs, projecting blame onto platforms while expanding its own authority.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Deception.
When you map the gap between protecting children and tracking every citizen, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. The system trades organic parental empowerment for centralized state control.

The Unavoidable Truth: Children are being harmed by predatory, addictive digital designs.
The Unavoidable Lie: Universal digital surveillance is the only way to keep children safe online.

Alethekanon:
The math of control is simple: find an unassailable victim, manufacture an absolute threat, and demand total oversight as the only solution. The EU Kids Act is a masterclass in paternalistic overreach.

Awwthekanon:
Our children deserve real protection, warm communities, and safe spaces to grow. But wrapping them in digital chains and tracking their every move isn't safety—it's just replacing one cage with another.

Brothekanon:
So to save kids from scrolling TikTok, everyone has to upload their passport to log into the internet? Yeah, that sounds totally reasonable and not dystopian at all. Good luck with that, Europe.

Spirithekanon:
"Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it." Proverbs 22:6 PASS
True protection is cultivated through moral guidance and community, not through the cold, watchful eye of a digital state.

Actual Article Body:
The European Union is moving to ban social media for under 13s across the bloc and impose restrictions on the digital technology for older children, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced Wednesday.

The move to develop EU-wide rules comes after several individual EU member states have introduced social media limits on teenagers amid a global push to restrict children’s access to social media. Australia became the first country in the world to ban social media for under 16s in December 2025.

“No social media under the age of 13. No personal account under the age of 15,” Von der Leyen said during her state of the union address in Strasbourg, France.

The EU would allow 13- and 14-year olds to have “mini accounts” with parental supervision and limited features, she added. The use of such accounts would be capped at one hour per day.
